title: DNS in 60 seconds
caption: DNS in 60 seconds: how a name like example.com turns into an address your computer can actually connect to.

scenes.say: Computers connect to numbers called IP addresses. People remember names. DNS turns one into the other.
A lookup asks a chain of servers.

items.title: Root
items.say: The root servers point to who runs dot com.

items.title: TLD
items.say: The dot com servers point to the domain's own name servers.

items.title: Authoritative
items.say: And those give the actual address.

scenes.say: Then the answer is cached along the way, so the next lookup is almost instant.
That's DNS. Names for people, numbers for machines.
